paraphrase: Kabīr, a weaver's son refused as a disciple, lay on the steps of the ghāṭ before dawn; Rāmānanda, going down to bathe, stepped on him and cried 'Rām!'; Kabīr took this as his initiation into the Name.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). The story is standard in the popular and Rāmānandī accounts; its exact form in Anantadās is recalled only in outline.

location.ref: Kabīr Paracaī, the trial before Sikandar Lodī

paraphrase: Accused by brahmins and qāzīs before Sultan Sikandar, Kabīr refuses to bow; he is chained and thrown into the river, into fire and before an elephant, and survives each ordeal, until the Sultan asks his pardon.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Legend; recorded as the tradition's account.
